item.title: Bunny Levine, "Gilmore Girls" and "La La Land" actress, dies at 97
item.description:
Amanda Edwards / Amanda Edwards, Getty Images Bunny Levine, known for her roles in Gilmore Girls and La La Land , has died at 97, peacefully in her sleep. She passed Thursday in her Tarzana, California home, from what appears to have been natural causes. Before launching her Hollywood career in the late 1980s, Levine was a school librarian and teacher in Teaneck, New Jersey, for about 25 years. She has appeared in some of television’s biggest shows, including Everybody Loves Raymond , Law & Order , Ugly Betty , Private Practice , Criminal Minds , New Girl , and The Mindy Project . Levine has also acted in comedy movies You Don’t Mess With the Zohan , Sandy Wexler and You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah . item.title: Trump Imposes Harmful and Illegal Section 338 Tariffs Against Many Canadian Imports
item.description:
NA Yesterday, Donald Trump imposed massive 50% tariffs on numerous Canadian imports after trade negotiations with Canada broke down, largely due to the Trump administration's insistence on maintaining earlier 50% tariffs on Canadian aluminum products and other goods. Section 338 was a part of the notorious Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930, which gravely exacerbated the Great Depression. In a previous post , I summarized the reasons why Section 338 tariffs are an illegal usurpation of congressional authority by the president. As Philip Zelikow of the conservative Hoover Institution explained in a guest post here at the VC blog, last year, Section 338 was superseded by new legislation enacted in 1962 and 1974, and is therefore defunct. A United States Postal Service mail collection box is seen on a street in New York City, United States, on August 7, 2026. —Marcin Golba—NurPhoto The United States Postal Service (USPS) on Friday issued a 95-page final rule that it plans to implement immediately if the government obtains relief from two existing injunctions. item.description:
President Trump is reaching deeper into individual markets to try to ease consumer price strains . Why it matters: The administration is under mounting pressure to deliver relief as affordability becomes a bigger political liability ahead of the midterms.
